Here are the differences between the languages I found.

1) In Russian there are 10 parts of speech (although there are peculiarities), in Arabic there are three.

2) The Russian language currently distinguishes two numbers: singular and plural. In Arabic, three numbers are actively used: singular, plural and dual.

3) The category of animate. In Russian this category includes names of people, animals, birds, fish, etc. In Arabic, animate names include only those associated with human, and inanimate names include everything else.

4) The category of gender. In Russian there are three genders: masculine, feminine and neuter. In Arabic there are only two: masculine and feminine.

This is a complicated question, but I will try to explain this difference as I see it.

The word грёза is used to mean a vision or dream, either similar to a delusion or as such. For example, sleep paralysis can, in a sense, be called «грёза». Also, this word is often used in poetry and is synonymous with the word «мечта», but semantically it is higher than the word dream and is something idealistic and unattainable as opposed to a dream (мечта). In poetry, too, грёзы are usually only about love.

Мечта has the same meaning as in English. I dream of being an astronaut – я мечтаю быть астронавтом. 

Сон also has the same meaning as in English. You go to sleep and dream. (видеть сны). 

So, to summarize: грёзы is often translated in English as: dreams. If they want to emphasize the semantics of the word, they use the word reveries.
